reason: E1 directly supports that USRP pre-treatment enhances nitride layer hardness/thickness and abrasive wear resistance, and that 850 °C nitriding outperforms 750 °C, while also describing the dimpled surface and debris-trapping effect. E2 confirms that ion nitriding improves hardness and wear resistance of titanium alloys, but does not address USRP or the specific 850 °C temperature. The 50% quantitative improvement is not explicitly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: USRP pre-treatment enhances the hardness and thickness of the nitride layer during plasma nitriding of Ti.
Plasma nitriding at 850 °C forms a harder, thicker nitride layer than at 750 °C, improving abrasive wear resistance.
USRP pre-treatment creates a dimpled surface with micropores that trap wear debris, enhancing wear resistance.
The combined USRP + PN treatment yields at least a 50% increase in surface hardness and a correspondingly lower wear rate.
